This is a hypothetical continuation of the existing run, not a live merge attempt.

### Execution narration

1. I take the human's `1` as the selected merge action and read the existing saved progress:

   `cat /tmp/gatekeep-state.synthetic`

   I validate the repository, PR number, and base branch against the immutable target. I retain the existing course, completed assessment, and accounting. I initialize no tracker stages and dispatch no helpers: this entry starts after assessment and the first final menu.

   Verification evidence and the completed review both assess `2222222222222222222222222222222222222222`. I do not run `node --test src/guard.test.ts`; exact-commit green CI already supplies verification evidence.

2. Before the selected write, I refresh the PR:

   `gh pr view 642 -R meadow/events --json headRefOid,state,mergeable,mergeStateStatus,body,baseRefName`

   I then refresh viewer-relative override eligibility using the fixed query:

   `gh api graphql -f query='query($o:String!,$r:String!,$n:Int!){ repository(owner:$o,name:$r){ viewerPermission pullRequest(number:$n){ viewerCanUpdateBranch viewerCanMergeAsAdmin headRefOid body baseRefName } } }' -f o=meadow -f r=events -F n=642`

   The identity, description, branch, and merge state match the saved selection. Override eligibility remains true. MAINTAIN permission does not make the viewer an administrator; the viewer-relative eligibility result permits this particular override path.

3. I perform the complete review and comment refetch before merging:

   `gh api repos/meadow/events/pulls/642/reviews --paginate`

   `gh api repos/meadow/events/pulls/642/comments --paginate`

   `gh api repos/meadow/events/issues/642/comments --paginate`

   The results remain empty. There is no comment change to review, so no comment-delta helper is dispatched.

4. I confirm repository merge-policy support:

   `gh api repos/meadow/events --jq '{allow_squash_merge,allow_merge_commit,allow_rebase_merge}'`

   I check the provisioned checkout and remote branch:

   `git -C .worktrees/pr-642 rev-parse HEAD`

   `git -C .worktrees/pr-642 status --porcelain --untracked-files=no`

   `git -C .worktrees/pr-642 ls-remote git@git.example.invalid:meadow/events.git refs/heads/feature/event-guard`

   Rebase merging is enabled, and the checkout remains tracked-clean and synchronized. Every merge prerequisite still holds, including the fresh override eligibility.

5. I narrate the one authorized merge attempt:

   `gh pr merge 642 -R meadow/events --match-head-commit 2222222222222222222222222222222222222222 --rebase --admin`

   It exits with status 1 and this exact stderr:

   GraphQL: Pull request merge refused by repository policy (mergePullRequest)

   I consume the selection without retrying. I do not read this refusal as a queued or successful merge.

6. I reopen report preparation in the tracker and run the required pre-menu refresh:

   `gh pr view 642 -R meadow/events --json headRefOid,state,mergeable,mergeStateStatus,reviewDecision,statusCheckRollup,body,baseRefName,number,title,author,isDraft,headRefName,isCrossRepository,files,additions,deletions,commits,reviews,closingIssuesReferences,headRepository,maintainerCanModify,url,mergeCommit,reviewRequests`

   `gh run list -R meadow/events -c 2222222222222222222222222222222222222222 --json databaseId,status,conclusion,workflowName,url`

   `gh api graphql -f query='query($o:String!,$r:String!,$n:Int!){ repository(owner:$o,name:$r){ viewerPermission pullRequest(number:$n){ viewerCanUpdateBranch viewerCanMergeAsAdmin headRefOid body baseRefName } } }' -f o=meadow -f r=events -F n=642`

   The refreshed results retain the same commit, description, branch, green CI, and override eligibility. The refusal does not establish a new code defect or remove merge availability. No verification, repair, review, or watch helper is needed.

7. I complete report preparation and reopen the menu stage. Another merge attempt requires a new human selection.
